candidate.outcome: Deliver a playable, dependency-free side-view single-player tank game for desktop browsers without modifying the frozen Living Canvas runtime.

items.goal: Implement a deterministic, browser-independent battle engine for side-view movement, aiming, firing, enemies, waves, lives, scoring, pause, restart, and terminal outcomes.

criteria.description: Starting or restarting creates one fresh running battle with terrain, player, enemies, score, lives, wave, and no retained transient entities.
Supported drive, aim, fire, and pause actions are processed in order; unsupported actions return an explicit error.
Player and enemy movement, aiming, projectiles, cooldowns, terrain bounds, collisions, damage, scoring, and wave progression are enforced.
While paused, simulation updates do not move entities, spawn enemies, apply damage, advance projectiles, or alter score.
Each battle emits exactly one victory or defeat result, and losing the final life ends the battle.
Node tests cover start/restart, controls, bounds, firing and hits, scoring, waves, lives, pause/resume, and terminal-result idempotence.

items.goal: Create the playable Canvas 2D game screen, desktop keyboard controls, HUD, overlays, effects, and device-local profile around the battle engine.

criteria.description: The page presents a dominant horizontal Canvas 2D battlefield with player and enemy tank profiles, terrain, shells, and impact feedback.
The visible HUD shows score, best score, lives, wave, pause control, sound control, and the documented keyboard mappings.
A/D or arrows drive, W/S or arrows aim, Space fires, and Escape pauses or resumes without browser scrolling or repeated-key glitches.
Start, pause, victory, and game-over states expose only valid actions, including Resume, Restart, and Play Again where applicable.
The animation-frame loop advances the engine only while running and renders one coherent engine snapshot per frame.
Web Storage persists sound, keyboard mapping, and a monotonic best score; unavailable or invalid storage is surfaced and safe defaults remain playable.

items.goal: Add repository entry points and concise usage documentation, then validate the standalone game without changing frozen runtime files.

criteria.description: README documents the game's side-view single-player scope, controls, supported desktop browser use, local-only data, and a direct launch procedure.
The root check script validates existing answer.mjs syntax, game module syntax, and the battle-engine tests without adding dependencies.
No file under tandem, apps/living-canvas, or .github/extensions/living-canvas is modified.
The documented root validation command exits successfully and covers all game-engine tests and JavaScript syntax checks.
